Inferred defensive scheme labels derived from PPP were near-uniform, suggesting label noise and inability to separate defensive changes from offensive execution, making this approach untestable with the current data.

evidence_establishes: Labeling of PNR and DRIVE play types in the dataset is unreliable and potentially biased; PPP estimates for these play types may be distorted by foul leakage and labeling errors.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a preceding DRIVE actually raises PNR PPP; no prior study has directly tested this sequencing effect with reliable labels.
own_inferences: The high labeling error for PNR and the foul leakage bias for DRIVE suggest that any observed effect of preceding DRIVE on PNR PPP could be an artifact unless labeling is improved or corrected.
uncertainties: Exact magnitude of the labeling error for DRIVE in the current dataset; the prevalence of preceding DRIVE possessions in the dataset; how to best correct for foul leakage in PPP calculations.
